THESE MISCELLANEOUS FIRST APPEALS, COMING ON FOR ORDERS, THIS DAY, UMESH M. ADIGA, J., DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 JUDGMENT Respondent No.2/Insurer in M.V.C.No.1209/2014 has filed M.F.A.No.200359/2017 and claimant in the said case has filed M.F.A.No.200981/2017.
Insurer in M.V.C.No. 1264/2014 has filed M.F.A.No.200360/2017 and claimants of that case have filed M.F.A.No.200982/2017.
The Insurer has challenged the quantum of compensation awarded as well as liability fastened on the Insurer to pay the compensation.
The claimants in both the cases have filed the appeals claiming for enhancement of compensation.
All the four appeals arises out of the common judgment and award dated 24.12.2016 passed in M.V.C.No.1209/2014 and M.V.C.No.1264/2014 on the file of the MACT-IV, Vijayapura.

M.V.C.No.1209/2014 and M.V.C.No.1264/2014 arises out of common accident and the Tribunal has taken up both the matters together, common evidence was recorded and passed common judgment.
2.
At the time of hearing on admission, with the consent of both the sides, these appeals are taken up for final disposal.
3. We refer the parties as per their rank before the Tribunal in M.V.C.No.1264/2014.
It is the case of the claimants that on 24.06.2014, deceased Channamma along with claimant No.1, were going on a motor cycle as a pillion rider and claimant No.2 was riding the said motor cycle.
They met with an accident on Sindagi-Vijayapur Road near Devara Hipparagi bus-stand, due to rash and negligent driving of the lorry bearing Reg.No.KA-21-A-1767, by its NC: 2023:KHC-K:5418-DB driver.
Due to the impact, Channamma had sustained grievous injuries and died at the spot.
Claimant No.1, who was aged about 2 years at the time of the accident, had sustained grievous injuries.
Claimants No.1 and 2 are daughter and husband respectively of deceased Channamma and Claimants No.3 and 4 are parents-in-law of the deceased.

sentences.text: Respondents have contended that they were depending upon the earnings of the deceased and prayed to award compensation of Rs.63 Lakhs.

4. The claimant in M.V.C.No.1209/2014 is none other than the minor daughter of late Channamma,
who has sustained grievous injuries, has filed the said petition contending that she had sustained grievous injuries in the accident and suffering from permanent disability to an extent of 32.5% and with these reasons, prayed to award compensation of Rs.36 Lakhs.
5.

Both the respondents, who are owner and Insurer of the offended lorry, have denied the contention of NC: 2023:KHC-K:5418-DB the claimants and they have contended that the accident had taken place due to rash and negligent riding of the motor cycle by claimant No.2 and driver of the lorry was not responsible for the accident.
The owner of the lorry has contended that the said vehicle was insured with Respondent No.2 and it is liable to pay compensation.

6. Respondent No.2/Insurer has contended that driver of the lorry had no valid and effective license to drive the lorry, at the time of the accident and the owner has violated terms and conditions of the policy of the insurance.
Therefore, it is not liable to indemnify the owner and prays to dismiss the claim petition against it.
7. The Tribunal, on tshe basis of rival contentions had framed necessary issues.
8. The claimants have examined PWs-1 to 4 and got marked Exs.P1 to P13.
Respondent No.2 examined RW-1 and got marked Ex.R1.
The Tribunal, after hearing both the parties and on appreciation of pleadings and evidence on record, by the impugned judgment partly allowed the claim petition.

The Tribunal has awarded the following compensation in M.V.C.No.1209/2014:

We have heard the arguments.
The learned Advocate for claimant has submitted that the Tribunal has not considered permanent disability of minor petitioner in M.V.C.No.1209/2014.

The Doctor has been examined,
who has assessed the disability at 32.5% to the entire body and that was not considered by the Tribunal.
the amount of compensation awarded under the other heads are meager.

Therefore,
prayed to enhance the compensation.

13. The learned Advocate for the claimants in M.V.C.No.1264/2014 has submitted that the deceased was a professional food-grain grader, aged about 22 years and her monthly income was Rs.15,000/-
to Rs.21,000/-.
The Tribunal without any reasons has not accepted it and assessed income of the deceased as Rs.4,500/- per month.
The Tribunal has not added future prospects to the said income and meager amount was awarded towards loss of dependency.
He has further submitted that compensation awarded towards loss of consortium is also very meager.
It is the evidence of PW-1 and Ex.P10 that deceased Channamma was pregnant of eight months.

Due to her - 12 - NC: 2023:KHC-K:5418-DB death, the fetus in the womb also died causing irreparable loss of a child to the claimant No.2 and claimant No.1 has also lost either a brother or sister who could be company to her, had Channamma survived.
The said loss has not been compensated by the Tribunal.
With these reasons, prayed to enhance the compensation.
14. The learned Advocate for the Insurer/Appellant has submitted that amount of compensation awarded in both the cases are on higher side.
It needs to be re- calculated.
She has further submitted that accident had taken place due to rash and negligent driving of motor cycle by claimant No.1, in M.V.C.No.1264/2019.
He had no license to ride the motor cycle.

Though this fact was raised before The Branch Manager, Oriental vs Mallappa And Ors on 17 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/124447455/
8 the Tribunal, the Tribunal has not considered it and did not hold that accident had taken place due to contributory negligence of rider of the motor cycle.

sentences.text:
Therefore, the impugned judgment needs to be set aside against Respondent No.2.
- 13 - NC: 2023:KHC-K:5418-DB 15. The following points emerges for our determination:
i) Whether the accident was caused due to contributory negligence of rider of the motor cycle, i.e., claimant No.2?
ii) Whether the claimants are entitled for enhancement of compensation?
16.
The fact of accident is not in dispute.
The Tribunal in detailed discussion has held that accident had taken place due to rash and negligent driving of lorry by its driver.
PW-1 was rider of the motor cycle and PW-2 was an eye-witness.
In their cross-examination, respondents were unable to bring out any admission to show that PW-1 was negligent in riding of the motor cycle or he had contributed for occurrence of the accident.
Moreover, it is not in dispute that the lorry had hit the rear side of the motor cycle and caused the accident.
It is not case of respondents that rider of motorcycle has suddenly applied break and hence, accident has taken place.
Under those circumstances, it is difficult to accept the submission of the learned Advocate for - 14 - NC: 2023:KHC-K:5418-DB the Insurer, that accident was due to contributory negligence.

Moreover,
the Insurer has not got impleaded owner and Insurer of the said motor cycle.

It is settled law that in the absence of owner and Insurer of the said vehicle, the Tribunal cannot asses the contributory negligence and direct the person who is not a party to the litigation, to pay the compensation.
Deceased Channamma and minor child, viz., Kirti are third parties.
They were not responsible for accident.
Hence, they can claim compensation from either of joint tort-feasors.

On this count also,
submission of the learned Advocate for the Insurer is not tenable.
17. The claimant in M.V.C.No.1209/2014 is a minor aged about two years.
She had sustained injuries such as head injury and brachial plexus (injury to the nerve roots in the cervical and upper trunk).
According to PW-3, the said child lost sensation over the upper limb and is also suffering from weakness of right upper limb.
The child was referred to NIMHANS Hospital, Bengaluru for treatment.
The child has been suffering from permanent disability of 32.05% as - 15 - NC: 2023:KHC-K:5418-DB per evidence PW-3.
The Tribunal has awarded compensation towards pain and suffering, medical expenses and loss of amenities, etc.
In all, it has awarded Rs.66,250/-.

sentences.text: The child is aged about two years, therefore, it is not possible to assess disability, which is affecting its earning capacity.
Even during the arguments of this case, the child must be aged about 10 to 11 years.
What is the status of health of the child is not placed on record.

Under the circumstances, the submission of the learned Advocate for the claimants that the child is entitled for compensation under the head 'loss of future earning capacity' due to permanent disability is not acceptable.

However, considering the facts and circumstances as well as the injury sustained by the said minor child, global compensation of Rs.25,000/- is awarded in addition to whatever awarded by the Tribunal.
19. It is the case of the petitioner in M.V.C.No. 1264/2014 that the deceased Channamma was aged about 22 years and earning Rs.15,000/- to Rs.21,000/- per month as food-grain grader.
The Tribunal accepted the age of the - 16 - NC: 2023:KHC-K:5418-DB deceased as 22 years, on the basis of the material available on record.

The Tribunal has rightly rejected the contention of the claimant that the deceased was earning Rs.15,000/- to Rs.21,000/- per month since there is lack of evidence, except self-serving statement of PW-1.
The Tribunal has taken the income of the deceased as Rs.4,500/-, per month which is on the lower side.

In case of settlement of motor vehicle claim petitions in the Lok-Adalath, for an accident taken place during the year 2014, notional income of the victim is considered as Rs.7,500/-
per month.
The same could be applied to the facts of the present case.
Admittedly, the multiplier applicable in this case is '18'.
40% of her income (Rs.3,000) has to be added towards future prospects since the deceased was aged about 22 years.
1/3rd of the earnings (Rs.3500) of the deceased has to be deducted towards her personal expenses.
Therefore, the claimants are entitled for compensation under the head 'loss of dependency' is (Rs.7000X12X18) = Rs.15,12,000/-.
The Tribunal has awarded Rs.20,000/- towards loss of love and affection and loss of consortium as Rs10,000/-.

In the case of (NATIONAL INSURANCE COMPANY LIMITED Vs. PRANAY SETHI AND OTHERS)1 and MAGMA GENERAL INSURANCE COMPANY LIMITED VS. NANU RAM ALIAS CHUHRU RAM AND OTHERS2, each claimants are entitled for Rs.40,000/- towards loss of consortium.

are entitled for Rs.80,000/- towards 'loss of consortium'.

Claimants are also entitled for enhancement of the compensation awarded by the Tribunal under the conventional heads, 'loss of estate and funeral expenses', i.e., Rs.15,000/-
each.
21.
In the evidence of PW-1 as well as in Ex.P4, it is stated that the deceased was pregnant of eight months.
She could have delivered the child within a short period, had she survived, but unfortunately died.

sentences.text: Claimant No.1 had lost company of a brother/sister.
The said loss of claimant No.1 cannot be quantified.
As per the cause-title, claimant No.2 is aged about 24 years at the time of the accident.
Thre is possiblity that he may marry again and lead marital life.
In that event, claimant No.1 has to live with the step-mother.
She may not get similar love and affection from step-mother that was given by natural mother.
The said child was two years at the time of death of her mother.
Had Channamma survived, the said claimant No.1 would have got brother or sister with whom she could share her happiness and sorrow and also enjoyed the company.
The said child lost the said joy due to the death of Channamma when she was pregnant of eight months.

Looking into the facts of this case, we deem it appropriate to award compensation of Rs.2,50,000/-, which shall be exclusively given to claimant No.1 and shall be deposited in her name till she attains the majority.
As already stated above, the said loss cannot be assessed in terms of money.
However, to console the grief of the child, the said amount of compensation is awarded.
For the aforesaid discussion, the following amount of compensation is awarded:

Sl. No. Particulars Amount  (Rs.)
 1. Loss of dependency 15,12,000  2. Loss of consortium 80,000  3. Loss of estate 15,000  4. Funeral expenses 15,000  5. Loss of joy due to death of child 2,50,000  in mother's womb to claimant  No.1  Total 18,72,000

Claimants in M.V.C.No.1264/2014 are entitled for enhancement of Rs.11,79,000/-.
23.

For the aforesaid discussion, we answer point No.1 in the negative and point No.2 partly in affirmative and pass the following:
ORDER i) The Appeals in M.F.A.No.200359 of 2017 and M.F.A.No.200360 of 2017 are dismissed.

- 20 - NC: 2023:KHC-K:5418-DB iii) The impugned judgment and award passed by the Tribunal in M.V.C.No.1209 of 2014 and M.V.C.No.1264 of 2014 dated 24.12.2016 is modified as under:
a) Claimant in M.V.C.No.1209 of 2014 is entitled for enhancement of global compensation of Rs.25,000/- without any interest to the said amount in addition to the amount awarded by the Tribunal.

b) Claimant in M.V.C.No.1264 of 2014  are entitled for compensation of  Rs.18,72,000 as against  Rs.6,93,000/- awarded by the Tribunal and claimants are entitled for enhancement of Rs.11,79,000/-
 with interest at the rate of 6% per  annum on the enhanced amount from the date of the petition till its realization.
c) The enhanced amount of compensation in M.V.C.No.1209s of 2014 shall be kept in fixed deposit in - 21 - NC: 2023:KHC-K:5418-DB the name of claimant No.1 till she attains the age of majority.

In the enhanced amount of compensation, in M.V.C.No.1264 of 2014, in addition to her share in the compensation, i.e., an amount of Rs.2,50,000/- shall be exclusively paid to claimant No.1, and same shall be kept in fixed deposit till she attain age of majority, in her name, in any of the nationalized Bank.
The remaining enhanced amount of compensation shall be apportioned in the ratio of 60:20:10:10.
The deposit and release of the amount shall be in term of the award passed by the Tribunal.

opennyai_summary.facts:
The Insurer has challenged the quantum of compensation awarded as well as liability fastened on the Insurer to pay the compensation.
The owner of the lorry has contended that the said vehicle was insured with Respondent No.2 and it is liable to pay compensation.
6. Respondent No.2/Insurer has contended that driver of the lorry had no valid and effective license to drive the lorry, at the time of the accident and the owner has violated terms and conditions of the policy of the insurance.
Therefore, it is not liable to indemnify the owner and prays to dismiss the claim petition against it.
opennyai_summary.arguments: He had no license to ride the motor cycle.

i) Whether the accident was caused due to contributory negligence of rider of the motor cycle, i.e., claimant No.2?
ii) Whether the claimants are entitled for enhancement of compensation?
16.
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
It is not case of respondents that rider of motorcycle has suddenly applied break and hence, accident has taken place.
Moreover,
the Insurer has not got impleaded owner and Insurer of the said motor cycle.
It is settled law that in the absence of owner and Insurer of the said vehicle, the Tribunal cannot asses the contributory negligence and direct the person who is not a party to the litigation, to pay the compensation.
Deceased Channamma and minor child, viz., Kirti are third parties.
They were not responsible for accident.
Hence, they can claim compensation from either of joint tort-feasors.

However, considering the facts and circumstances as well as the injury sustained by the said minor child, global compensation of Rs.25,000/- is awarded in addition to whatever awarded by the Tribunal.
40% of her income (Rs.3,000) has to be added towards future prospects since the deceased was aged about 22 years.
Therefore, the claimants are entitled for compensation under the head 'loss of dependency' is (Rs.7000X12X18) = Rs.15,12,000/-.
The Tribunal has awarded Rs.20,000/- towards loss of love and affection and loss of consortium as Rs10,000/-.
In the case of (NATIONAL INSURANCE COMPANY LIMITED Vs. PRANAY SETHI AND OTHERS)1 and MAGMA GENERAL INSURANCE COMPANY LIMITED VS. NANU RAM ALIAS CHUHRU RAM AND OTHERS2, each claimants are entitled for Rs.40,000/- towards loss of consortium.
Hence, only claimants No.1 and 2, who are minor daughter and husband of deceased together
are entitled for Rs.80,000/- towards 'loss of consortium'.
Claimants are also entitled for enhancement of the compensation awarded by the Tribunal under the conventional heads, 'loss of estate and funeral expenses', i.e., Rs.15,000/-
each.
